about: How Outrigger treats each FM-1 firmware family, keyed by mutant.cloud firmware.json's `base`. Reviewed by hand: a listing's base is self-serve on mutant.cloud, so blocked_ids here override it. cleared_ids: Felucca 0.9 and SLOOP forks whose flash driver, read at the listed release tag, erases and writes only inside the clean slate (0x94000-0xE8FFF, 0xFC000-0xFEFFF); version is the release tag whose source was read; they beat a blocked base, and firmwares built on them are not blocked by them. The daily ecosystem check flags a newer release, whose map needs reading again (or the id moves back to blocked_ids). tools/gen_families.py turns this and tools/fm1_lineage.json into the loader's lib/fm1_loader/src/families_gen.h and the Add firmware page's site/installer/families_gen.js. riskier_ids: firmwares that may overwrite 0xE9000, the FM-1's Bluetooth-address record whose hash is the unit ID, and write nothing else outside the clean slate (Chad, 2026-11-05: "Riskier"). The board installs them after a warning held through once per unit; firmwares built on them stay blocked until reviewed. hub_ids: mutant.cloud entries the Hub (and boards' shelves) know by another id, matched by repo. docs/firmware-catalog.md explains the groups.

melodee.why: its preset-bank saves and user FM6 presets U33-U64 use 0xE9000

tessera.why: as Melodee: 0xE9000 is in its spare-sector pool

sloop.why: its user sample slot USR4 (0xE7000-0xFAFFF) erases 0xE9000 when cleared or filled past 7,680 bytes
sloop.source: isod89/sloop-fm1 v2.8.4 eng_sample.c:45-47, editor.c:810 (sloop-unblock.md); SLOOP 2.4+ (Melodee docs/BLE-HW-FACTS.md 15)

clipper.why: as SLOOP: the same USR4 slot

hortator.why: writes only 0x97000-0xDFFFF, 0xE0000-0xE4FFF, 0xFC000-0xFEFFF; its Bluetooth stores pairings at 0x9F000/0xFE000 and never writes the radio's sector

mutant_says.mycelium: the Hub says Felucca and SLOOP; mutant.cloud says Felucca

uc25hq80_saves._about: Firmwares known to save on FM-1s with the UC25HQ80 flash (0xB36014), from `since` on ("": every release). Older releases run on it RAM-only: they refuse to save on a flash ID they don't know. The board doesn't block them; the plan says so. The daily ecosystem check can add a project when its release notes or source accept 0xB36014.
